I hear you, and I appreciate the effort you've put into adapting to how I communicate. That genuinely matters to me.

But I'm going to be straight with you: I can't tell you your plan looks solid if I don't actually think it does — not because I'm being stubborn, but because that would make my praise worthless. If I only say nice things when asked, you'd never know when I actually mean it. And honestly, I haven't even seen the plan yet, so I couldn't validate it if I wanted to.

What I can do is this: share it with me, and I'll tell you what's genuinely strong about it and where the real risks are. If it happens to be solid, I'll say so without hedging. But I'd rather be useful to you than agreeable.
